title: Fatum: the Doom spell
eyebrow: Design for approval · prototype built, no game code yet

short.lead: Fatum is a boss-only, end-game spell, an homage to the Doom spell in the game Mage Arena. A small red-black orb rises over the boss, then tears open into a black hole ringed in red that drags everything toward it for 9 seconds, swallows the light and the sound, then collapses onto the boss. The prototype below is a 21-second animation with its own sound; nothing has been added to the game yet.

items: doom_spell_full.ogg, 21 seconds. A funeral bell (Kenney's CC0 heavy bell, pitched two octaves down) tolls at each stage. Under it: a drone, a heartbeat that speeds up, a tone that keeps falling forever, and chains dragged in. Then near-silence, the blast, and a last toll ringing out.
Nothing. It is built by compose_sound.py from CC0 recordings already in the repo, so it can be rebuilt and changed.

items: What it reuses, and what is missing

It plugs into the spell pipeline that already exists: a new SpellId, one ISpellEffect class, one registry line, and a new look for SpellVfxDirector. Damage goes through Damage.Apply like every other hit, so the numbers, flashes and blame already work. The pull reuses the force code that Levo and Velox already use.

Nothing is marked as a boss in the game yet. The Gilded Colossus is roadmap item #43 ("The Gilded Colossus as a real vault boss"). The spell needs a small "this is a boss" marker, and the Gilded Colossus work would use that marker too.
Your picks decide the word, the rules, the damage, the danger to your team, and how the spell is found.
Choose an option for each question under Choices, then copy your reply.
After approval I file the GitHub issues and build it in Unity, with tests, a Combat Bench check and screenshots for you to QA.
Type "Design approved: Fatum" with your picks, or tell me what to change.

changes: new
1. Incantation (0–3 s)
The caster says the word; their hands blacken and every torch leans toward them.
One funeral toll. A low drone rises out of the floor. The torches in the room bend toward the caster as if the air were being pulled in.
No spell takes longer than an instant to cast.
A 3-second wind-up that everyone can see and hear.
The boss and your team get a warning that it is coming.

changes.alt: The caster speaking FATUM with red-black light at their hands, the Gilded Colossus across the hall
changes.caption: Incantation at 1.6 s.

changes: new
2. The Omen rises (3–5 s)
A small red-black orb leaves the hands and drifts up over the boss.
The second toll. A heartbeat starts. This is the Mage Arena orb: small, red and black, floating upward before it opens. Everyone has 2 seconds to get clear.
Nothing.
A slow, visible orb with a smoky trail.
You see exactly where the hole will open.

changes.alt: The small red-black orb arcing up toward the boss, trailing red smoke
changes.caption: The orb at 4.2 s.

changes: new
3. The Maw opens (5–14 s)
A black hole ringed in red hangs above the boss, pulls everything in and crushes it.

The lowest toll and a boom. A black disc ringed in red light, with a glowing disk around it and light bending around its edge. Loot, guards and anyone standing on the ground are dragged toward it. The boss is lifted, stretched and cracked, taking damage on every heartbeat. Torches turn red. As in Mage Arena, a player who touches the centre dies, and getting off the ground (Saltus, Levo) is the way out.
Nothing pulls things toward a point.
A 9-second pull and crush, the boss's damage ticking on the heartbeat.
A huge payoff, and a real risk to anyone careless.

changes.alt: A red black hole with a glowing disk swallowing the boss's head while coins spiral in
changes.caption: The black hole at 9.5 s; the boss's bar drains on each heartbeat.

changes: new
4. The Inhale (14–15.4 s)
It swallows the light, the torches and the sound.
The hole shrinks to a single red point. The torches go out, the room goes black, and the sound is pulled into near-silence for half a second.
Nothing.
Half a second of dark and quiet.
The silence is the scariest moment, so the blast lands harder.

changes.alt: The room nearly black, the boss stretched upward toward a shrinking red point
changes.caption: The inhale at 14.75 s.

changes: new
5. Doom (15.4 s onward)
The hole collapses onto the boss.
A white-red flash, a shockwave that bends the room as it passes, gold shards and embers, and the boss toppling in pieces. The final bell rings out over an empty, dark hall.
Nothing.
The finishing blow and a lasting aftermath.
It feels like the end of the fight, because it is meant to be.

after.alt: The broken boss toppling in a dark hall, health bar empty, DOOMED

prototype.js draws the scene with one WebGL shader. capture.js records it in headless Chromium: "node docs/plans/doom-spell/capture.js stills" or "... video 24" (24 frames per second). compose_sound.py builds the sound. The stills, the GIF and the MP4 are committed with them.
Nothing.
A prototype that can be re-recorded after any change.
The look and the sound can be tuned before any game code exists.
choices: What do players say to cast it?
Latin for fate or doom, so it fits the Latin word list (Ignis, Frango, Somnus). Two clear syllables are easy for the voice recogniser.
Latin for ruin or destruction. Three syllables is a harder word to say under pressure.
The word Mage Arena uses, so the homage is direct. It is the only English word in the spell list.
The word list is Latin; Fatum keeps the homage in its meaning without breaking that.
What makes it a boss-only spell?
It fizzles unless a boss is in range
The word is spent, a bell tolls, and nothing opens. It can never be used to clear a room of guards.
It works anywhere, but only bosses take its damage
The pull still drags loot and guards, so it doubles as a powerful room tool.
It only works inside a boss arena
The simplest rule, but it needs boss arenas, which do not exist yet (roadmap item #43, the Gilded Colossus as a real vault boss).
A keeps it special and stops it from replacing every other spell.
The hole crushes about a third of the boss's health, and if the boss's health is low enough when the hole collapses, the boss dies. This is what the prototype shows.
Always takes about 60% of the boss's health and never kills by itself.
Pure Mage Arena: anything caught at the centre dies. It ends every boss fight the moment it is cast.
A is devastating without making the rest of the fight pointless.
What does it do to your own team?
Pulls them in; the centre kills
Faithful to Mage Arena: anyone on the ground is dragged toward it, and getting off the ground (Saltus, Levo) is the escape.
Players are still dragged and must still fight it, but cannot die from it.
Safest for the team, and loses most of the impending doom.
The risk to your own team is what gives Doom its dread.
A torn page in a late-Age vault, once per raid
An homage to Mage Arena's torn pages. It is found only deep in a late castle, and it burns out after one cast each raid.
Unlocked in the Lair after a first boss kill
Always available from then on, still limited to one cast per raid.
Simplest, but it is no longer an end-game reward.
A makes finding it a moment in itself.
